steps.label: Potassium (Z = 19)
lines: Potassium has atomic number 19, so it
The orbitals fill in order of rising
steps.why: The configuration is built by filling orbitals in order of rising energy until all 19 electrons are placed. The 4s orbital lies below 3d in energy, so the last electron enters 4s and potassium ends with one outer s electron.
common_mistakes: Writing 3d¹ for the last electron. The 4s orbital is lower in energy than 3d, so 4s fills first.
Stopping at 3p⁶, which is only 18 electrons. Potassium has 19.
steps.memory_tip: Fill up to argon, which is 18 electrons, then add the nineteenth in 4s.
steps.margin_note: Add the superscripts; they must total 19.

steps.label: Lithium (Z = 3)
lines: Lithium has atomic number 3, so it has
Both metals end in ns¹, which is the
steps.why: Two electrons fill the 1s orbital and the third goes into 2s, so lithium also ends in a single outer s electron. That shared ns¹ ending is why lithium and potassium are placed in the same group.
common_mistakes: Writing 1s³. An s orbital holds two electrons at most.
The shorthand [He] 2s¹ is correct chemistry, but this question asks for the complete form, so write every subshell out.
steps.memory_tip: Lithium is helium's pair plus one 2s electron, written out in full as 1s² 2s¹.
steps.margin_note: Write every subshell out; the question asks for the complete form.

insider_note: Check each configuration by adding the superscripts: they must come to the atomic number, 19 for potassium and 3 for lithium.
